ai.definition: Neural prosthetics are advanced brain-computer interfaces designed to directly interact with the brain’s neural networks for restoring lost functions such as movement or cognitive abilities, or enhancing human capabilities.
ai.howItWorks: These devices work by embedding electrodes into the brain tissue, which can record and stimulate neural activity. This allows them to interpret brain signals and translate these into commands that control external devices or directly modulate brain function.
ai.problemSolved: They address issues related to paralysis, sensory loss, and cognitive impairments, providing a means for individuals with neurological conditions to regain independence and functionality.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves the precise design and fabrication of microelectrode arrays that can be safely implanted into the brain. Materials must be biocompatible and capable of long-term stable operation within the body.
ai.buildProcess: The process includes designing the electrode array, fabricating it with appropriate materials, testing its functionality in vitro, and then conducting extensive safety and efficacy tests before clinical trials.
ai.costDrivers: High costs are driven by the need for advanced microfabrication techniques, biocompatible materials, and rigorous preclinical testing. Additionally, the complexity of integrating these devices with the brain’s intricate neural networks adds to the expense.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to transition from early clinical trials into broader commercial availability as regulatory hurdles are cleared and more evidence of safety and efficacy is gathered.
ai.regulation: Regulatory approval processes are stringent, requiring extensive testing for safety and effectiveness. This includes both animal studies and human clinical trials.
ai.risks: Risks include potential side effects such as infection, tissue damage, and long-term adverse reactions to implanted devices. There are also ethical concerns regarding the use of brain interfaces.
ai.profitability: Profitability is currently speculative but could be significant if the technology gains widespread adoption in both medical and consumer markets.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include miniaturization of components, improved biocompatibility, and better integration with other technologies such as artificial intelligence for more sophisticated control systems.

glossary.def: A system that enables direct communication between the brain and external devices.
Devices designed to replace or augment lost neural functions by interfacing directly with the brain's neural networks.

subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: the electrodes that either record the electrical chatter of neurons or deliver small currents to them.
parts: penetrating silicon microelectrode arrays (shanks tens of micrometres thick)
subdural ECoG grids placed on the brain surface
stimulation contacts (e.g. inside the cochlea or on the retina)

subsystems.name: Implant electronics
subsystems.role: amplify, filter and digitise faint neural signals inside the body.

subsystems.name: Power and telemetry
subsystems.role: gets power in and data out without a wire through the skin.

subsystems.name: Decoder
subsystems.role: turns patterns of neural activity into commands.

subsystems.name: External effector
subsystems.role: the limb, cursor or stimulator the user actually controls.

subsystems.name: Surgical delivery system
subsystems.role: places delicate electrodes precisely without damaging tissue.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Photolithography patterns metal traces onto silicon shanks or thin polymer films, then an insulating layer is added and only the tips are left exposed.

buildSteps.title: Package the electronics
buildSteps.detail: An amplifier and radio chip are sealed into a biocompatible case with hermetic feedthroughs, since body fluid destroys ordinary electronics.

buildSteps.title: Test and sterilise
buildSteps.detail: Each array is checked for electrode impedance and signal quality, then sterilised.

buildSteps.title: Plan and perform surgery
buildSteps.detail: Imaging and electrophysiology map the target area; a small opening in the skull allows the array to be inserted into or laid on the cortex.

buildSteps.title: Link wirelessly
buildSteps.detail: An external coil on the scalp powers and communicates with the implant through the skin.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the decoder
buildSteps.detail: The user attempts or imagines movements while neural activity is recorded; a model learns the mapping from activity to intent.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: The decoded command drives a limb or cursor, and feedback — visual, or increasingly touch — lets the user refine control.

buildSteps.title: Maintain over years
buildSteps.detail: Performance is monitored; signal loss from scarring or electrode movement is the main long-term failure mode.

prerequisites.why: scar tissue builds around penetrating electrodes and recordings fade over months to years.
pacemakers and cochlear implants show decade-scale sealing is achievable, but not yet at high channel counts.
hundreds of channels must stream data without cooking the tissue.
decoding intended movement works in research participants; robustness across days and users is still limited.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory and clinical pathway for brain implants
prerequisites.why: some devices are approved for specific conditions, but general-purpose cortical interfaces are still experimental.

pathway.milestone: cochlear implants and deep brain stimulation in routine clinical use
pathway.unlocks: millions of people hear or control tremor with implanted electronics.

pathway.milestone: fully implanted, wireless motor BCIs in larger clinical trials
pathway.unlocks: paralysed users controlling computers and robotic arms without a cable through the skull.

pathway.milestone: bidirectional interfaces that return touch and proprioception
pathway.unlocks: natural-feeling control of a prosthetic hand.
wider use in stroke, spinal injury and sensory loss.

pathway.milestone: cognitive or memory augmentation in healthy people
pathway.unlocks: claimed but unproven; the biology and the ethics are unresolved.
